The registry `Thread`'s stop button is `ComposerPrimitive.Cancel`. In the main composer it calls `cancelRun`, and `LocalRuntime` then fires the `abortSignal` passed to your `ChatModelAdapter.run`.

Your backend can find out through the request closing. Pass `abortSignal` to `fetch` (`signal: abortSignal`) or to your SDK call. Your server then sees the request close. It should pass its own request signal on to the model call so generation stops too. The docs' example is `abortSignal: req.signal` in an AI SDK route.

The `LocalRuntime` page also advises swallowing `AbortError`, since it means the user cancelled, and rethrowing other errors.

The docs I read don't say whether `LocalRuntime` sends any separate cancel message to your backend, or how server or proxy setups affect detecting the closed request.

Pages: docs/concepts/runtime.md, docs/concepts/messages.md, docs/runtimes/custom/local-runtime.md

Yes. **`AssistantModal`** is a ready-made bubble for support widgets and help desks. A fixed corner button opens a popover containing a full `Thread`, with a thread list, a new-thread button and a resizable window.

Import it from `@/components/assistant-ui/elements/assistant-modal.aui` and render it once under `AssistantRuntimeProvider`. It takes no props, has no standalone version, and opens automatically on `thread.runStart`. There's no `open` prop or ref, so to open it from another button, edit your copy to lift its `open`/`setOpen` state. You can restyle it with classes such as `aui-modal-content`.

There's also **Launcher**, a smaller panel with a greeting and starter prompts. Standalone `LauncherBubble` takes `open`, `unread`, `greeting`, `prompts` and callbacks that you wire up. Its runtime version uses `ThreadPrimitive.Suggestion` and `ComposerPrimitive.Send`; you track unread counts yourself.

The pages I read don't say how to install either one.

First, give your runtime a dictation adapter: `useChatRuntime({ adapters: { dictation: new WebSpeechDictationAdapter() } })`. Its options are `language`, `continuous` and `interimResults`. It uses the browser's speech recognition; the page lists Chrome, Edge and Safari. For server-rendered apps, check `WebSpeechDictationAdapter.isSupported` through `useSyncExternalStore`, with a `false` server snapshot.

Then, inside `ComposerPrimitive.Root`, add `ComposerPrimitive.Dictate` around a mic icon and `ComposerPrimitive.StopDictation` around a stop icon. Toggle them with `AuiIf`, checking whether `s.composer.dictation` is null. `Dictate` is disabled without an adapter.

Interim text previews in the input; final text is committed. `ComposerPrimitive.DictationTranscript` can display interim text separately. For errors such as `not-allowed`, read `s.composer.lastDictationEnd` with `useAuiState`.

For other transcription services, implement `DictationAdapter`; the page includes a `MediaRecorder` and server-route example. The page's wiring examples only use `useChatRuntime`.

Your store only needs `setMessages` if you want **branch switching**. The only required handler is `onNew`.

UI features turn on based on which callbacks you provide. Providing `setMessages: (messages: readonly T[]) => void` turns on branching, and it "performs branch switches." My reading is that because you own the state, switching branches means your store has to update what's visible. In one docs example, the callback is `setVisibleMessages(messages)`.

- **Branch trees:** A plain `messages` array treats each message's parent as the previous one. For branching, such as multiple regenerations, the docs pass a `messageRepository` with explicit `id` and `parentId` values, plus `setMessages`.
- **Related callbacks:** `unstable_onBranchChange` doesn't enable switching by itself. Editing needs `onEdit`, regeneration needs `onReload`, and `thread.import()` needs `onImport`.

The troubleshooting section also lists missing `setMessages` under "State not updating," but the docs don't say why. They also don't explain its internal mechanics.

Pages: docs/runtimes/custom/external-store.md

Pass a suggestion adapter as `useLocalRuntime(myChatModel, { adapters: { suggestion } })`. Its `generate({ messages })` runs after every assistant turn. Return suggestions shaped `{ prompt, title?, label? }`, either through a promise or through an async generator for streaming updates. The docs don't say whether each yield replaces or appends to the list.

For LLM-generated follow-ups, use `createSuggestionAdapter({ complete, count: 3 })`. `complete({ prompt, signal })` sends the transcript prompt it builds to your backend and, in the example, returns a string array. Forward `signal` to allow cancellation. Suggestions clear when a new run starts. To regenerate for an already-settled reply when adapter inputs change, change the adapter's `key`.

Results appear in `thread.suggestions`. Render them with `ThreadPrimitive.Suggestions`, but remove any static `Suggestions(...)` config, which stops it showing runtime ones. For follow-up chips, the registry ships `ThreadFollowupSuggestions`. For custom layouts, read `useAuiState((s) => s.thread.suggestions)`, and don't gate display on `thread.isEmpty`.

Pages: docs/guides/suggestions.md, docs/runtimes/custom/local-runtime.md

The docs MCP server is hosted at `https://www.assistant-ui.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP), with nothing to install.

- **Claude Code:** run `claude mcp add --transport http assistant-ui https://www.assistant-ui.com/mcp`.
- **Other IDEs:** `npx assistant-ui@latest mcp` configures the client.
- **Manual setup:** in `.cursor/mcp.json`, add the URL as `url` under `mcpServers`, then enable it in Cursor's MCP settings. Windsurf uses `serverUrl`. VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json` uses `servers` with `type: "http"` and `url`; enable MCP and use Copilot Chat in Agent mode.
- **Zed and Claude Desktop:** these use the local stdio proxy, run as `npx -y @assistant-ui/mcp-docs-server` in their config files.

Your agent then gets tools including `search_docs`, `read_page` and `list_pages`. If the connection fails, check network access, the exact URL and Streamable HTTP support. For stdio, check `npx`, then restart the server and IDE.

Pages: docs/llm.md

To render reasoning yourself, use the `MessagePrimitive.Parts` render function and return your component when `part.type === "reasoning"`. By default, reasoning renders nothing.

To group it, use `MessagePrimitive.GroupedParts` with `groupBy={groupPartByType({ reasoning: ["group-chainOfThought", "group-reasoning"], "tool-call": [...] })}`. Render `<MyReasoning {...part} />` for the `reasoning` case, and wrap `children` in group cases. Adjacent reasoning and tool calls share the outer group; text closes it. This is recommended for new code, even if your wrapper is a chain-of-thought accordion.

The legacy `components.ChainOfThought` prop takes over all reasoning and tool-call rendering, once per adjacent run. It's mutually exclusive with `Reasoning`, `ReasoningGroup`, `ToolGroup` and `tools`. Inside it, pass your renderer to `ChainOfThoughtPrimitive.Parts` as `components.Reasoning`, which receives `text` (this `components` prop is also deprecated). It starts collapsed, but `Parts` doesn't enforce that: gate it with `AuiIf` on `!s.chainOfThought.collapsed`. The docs don't say what happens if you omit `components.Reasoning`.

Pages: docs/guides/chain-of-thought.md, docs/primitives/message.md, docs/primitives/chain-of-thought.md
